clue.text: A sign of emptiness largely in conspirator in film

indicators.note: the A and the shortened word sit inside the conspirator's name

parts.note: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a blank space signals that nothing is there

explanation.surface: A plotter shows some sign of emptiness inside a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Casca is the plotter from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar; the second 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1942 Bogart and Bergman picture is one of the best-known Hollywood movies.

clue.text: 8 possibly supplying tip about book

indicators.note: the hint goes round the book's letter

parts.note: a cue is a hint or tip

explanation.surface: Eight, perhaps, giving a hint about a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' is a number here, not the cross-reference to 8-down it seems to be: 8 is two multiplied by itself thrice.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight equals two to the third power, an example of a number raised to the power three.

clue.text: Patron, perhaps lacking manners, left pastry

parts.note: a patron saint, abbreviated ST
rude means impolite

explanation.surface: An impolite customer departed, leaving a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patron' suggests a customer, but here it is a patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled layered Austrian dessert of thin dough, often filled with apple.

clue.text: Rely on say number in police showing an indication of interest?

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
to state is to say

indicators.note: the number's letter goes inside the police abbreviation

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Trust in a certain figure within the police force showing curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's police force. 'interest' is money earned, not curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A document from a lender listing transactions shows the interest accrued on an account.

clue.text: Early end to trip in island

indicators.note: tripping means stumbling, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An early finish to a journey on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to trip' rearranges EARLY END.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Channel Islands, between England and France.

clue.text: Victor once, say, getting firm aid for speaker

parts.note: CO is short for company
a mic, or microphone, helps a speaker be heard

explanation.surface: A winner of old gets company help to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victor was a British boys' paper of 1961-1992; 'Victor' looks like a winner or the V of radio code.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly strip-cartoon publication is an example of a children's periodical, now defunct.

clue.text: Was treating journalist high up in NY Times?

parts.note: anything in a New York paper is American, abbreviated US
an editor, abbreviated ED, is the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A query about a reporter getting high on drugs while working at the New York Times.
explanation.walkthrough: A top journalist at an American paper would be a 'US ED'; 'high up' points to rank, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone in a certain way, often badly, is to exploit or employ them.

clue.text: Unusual fear among group in phenomenon coming inland?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the group word

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd fear among a group about something arriving onshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges FEAR to EAFR, which goes 'among' SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sea mist that rolls in from the coast, especially in eastern England.

clue.text: Get ready to change rental agreement and arrangement at work?

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: Preparing to alter a tenancy deal and a workplace arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges READY.
explanation.definitionFit: A British scheme whereby employers let staff off work for study, an arrangement made by the workplace.

clue.text: Peer having produced nothing, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is said aloud and a like-sounding word is entered

parts.note: barren land or a barren effort yields nothing

explanation.surface: A lord who has achieved nothing, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, and this is one of its ranks.

clue.text: Protest by drivers in Mediterranean island — expression of popular will?

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: the motorists' club goes inside the island's abbreviation

parts.note: CY is the abbreviation for Cyprus
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Motorists stage a demonstration on a Mediterranean island to voice what the people want.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motoring club, here 'drivers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by vote of the people is a system expressing the general will of citizens.

clue.text: Period for peacefulness following disorder?

parts.note: a disorder is an illness; the quiet time after it is spent recovering

explanation.surface: A time of calm after public chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' suggests riot, but it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovery time after sickness, a gradual return to health.

clue.text: I discern trust that's collapsed in care provider

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: I perceive a failed health trust inside a care organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's collapsed' rearranges I DISCERN TRUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A community nurse who visits patients at home provides health care locally.

clue.text: Fancy European ship in waterway almost straying from point

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: the European and ship letters go inside the shortened waterway
most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a river is a waterway
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: An elegant European ship on a waterway nearly drifts off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RIVER to RIVE; ESS goes 'in' after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering off the subject, rambling away from the main topic.

clue.text: Unlucky backing for store around flat that's demolished

indicators.note: the reversed shop surrounds the jumbled letters
backing means the word for the shop runs from right to left

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Unfortunate support for a shop near a block of flats that's been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but is just the anagram fodder; the reversed shop splits after its second letter to take the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomed and unfortunate are synonyms: something destined for bad luck.

clue.text: Fluster conductor

definitions.meaning: to fluster is to unsettle or make nervous
Sir Simon ... is a celebrated British orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: Unsettle the person on the podium.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve is the verb sense; the surname of the leader of the London Symphony and Berlin Philharmonic is the other.

clue.text: Sinister adviser limiting reckless Russian leader?

indicators.note: cutting short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: rash means reckless
Vladimir Putin is the Russian president

explanation.surface: A malign counsellor restrains a reckless Kremlin chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' clips RASH to RAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The mystic monk who influenced the Romanov court is the classic malign advisor.

clue.text: Stick that is right for weapon

parts.note: rap, like stick, means criticism, as in 'take the rap' or 'get stick'
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A stick, that's to say, right for a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a club but means blame or criticism, as does RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender thrusting sword is a fencing blade.

clue.text: Type of minor claim largely blocked by term in insurance

indicators.note: the shortened word is stopped up by a letter put inside it
most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to pretend is to claim falsely

indicators.note: a term is an end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A kind of small claim, partly obstructed by a clause in a policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts PRETEND to PRETEN; 'term in' gives E, the last letter of insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A child just short of the teenage years, an example of someone under age.

clue.text: Wee payment put back for transport

parts.note: wee is slang for urine, or water

indicators.note: means the word for the payment is written backwards

parts.note: a sub is a subscription payment

explanation.surface: A child's toilet charge is refunded for travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns SUB into BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger boat running a regular service along a river is a means of travel.

clue.text: Principally, brilliant astronauts Armstrong perhaps and the remainder?

indicators.note: chiefly, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: Lance Armstrong, the cyclist

explanation.surface: Mainly, brilliant spacemen like Armstrong and the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armstrong' suggests Neil the astronaut, but it is the cyclist Lance.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum left over, as the amount still owed or the rest of something.

clue.text: Operatic style devised in keeping with stock character

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manner of opera was invented to fit a standard role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges OPERATIC STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conventional and clichéd fits a fixed, oversimplified type such as a stock figure.

clue.text: Sign voucher

definitions.meaning: a mark or symbol standing for something
a gift coupon exchangeable for goods

explanation.surface: Endorse a coupon.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a symbol of something and a gift coupon carry this word.

clue.text: Medical device not new? Restorative direction needed

indicators.note: the new letter is absent from the device

parts.note: a stent is a tube inserted to keep a vessel open

explanation.surface: A medical device that's old needs a healing instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restorative' sounds medical but this is the proofreader's mark: let a deleted text stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreading instruction meaning let it stand, restoring text marked for deletion.

clue.text: Study image in computing that's formulaic

indicators.note: the room and carving go inside the computing abbreviation

parts.note: IT is information technology
a den is a study or private room
a tiki is a carved Polynesian image of a human figure

explanation.surface: Examine a picture used in computers that follows a template.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' is a room, not a verb; 'image' is the Maori carving TIKI.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical and stereotyped, as if assembled from a standard kit of parts.

clue.text: Piece for group denied web access?

parts.note: no is a refusal
the net is the internet, the way onto the web

explanation.surface: A query about a band without internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 2,3 the answer reads as having no internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for nine players, as a quartet is for four.

clue.text: Make for audience flier

indicators.note: for listeners, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Produce something for listeners to hear about a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea eagle is a bird, hence a flier.

clue.text: How one might describe a decathlete's skill no matter what?

definitions.text: How one might describe a decathlete's skill
definitions.meaning: a ten-event athlete would be expected to be good at any of the disciplines

explanation.surface: Praising an all-round athlete's ability whatever the circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: A decathlon has ten events, so a competitor's skill shows at every one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means anyway or regardless; read literally it applies to an athletic contest.
